subtitle: When Mewar Faced Malwa and a Sultan Rode Home in Defeat

panels.shot: epic split-diagonal composition, low-angle, with two opposing figures dominating either half of the frame
panels.action: On one side Rana Kumbha sits tall in war gear on a massive horse before a rugged hill-fort skyline, on the other Mahmud Khalji in rich armour rides out from the plateau of Mandu, the plains of Malwa stretching between them under a stormy sky.

dialogue.text: In 1437, at Sarangpur, Rana Kumbha broke Malwa’s advance and, some say, took Sultan Mahmud Khalji alive—yet stone and chronicle remember that moment in different voices.

i18n.hi: १४३७ में सारंगपुर पर राणा कुम्भा ने मालवा की बढ़त तोड़ी और, कहते हैं, सुल्तान महमूद ख़िलजी को ज़िंदा पकड़ लिया – पर पत्थर और पुरालेख इस पल को अलग‑अलग तरह से याद करते हैं।

panels.shot: wide aerial over the plateau of Mandu and the Aravalli hills, contrasting two realms
panels.action: The camera looks down on the fortified capital of Mandu perched on its plateau while, far to the west, the rugged Aravalli hills cradle the hill forts of Mewar in a hazy dawn.

dialogue.text: In mid-fifteenth century India, two powers watched each other across plains and hills—Malwa from the plateau of Mandu, and Mewar from her stone crowns in the Aravallis.

i18n.hi: पंद्रहवीं सदी के बीच के भारत में दो ताकतें मैदानों और पहाड़ियों के आरपार एक‑दूसरे को देखती थीं – पठारी मण्डू से मालवा, और अरावली की पत्थरी चोटियों से मेवाड़।

panels.shot: medium interior shot in Mandu’s audience hall, slightly low angle toward Mahmud Khalji
panels.action: Mahmud Khalji stands in a carved hall in Mandu, hand resting on a map spread over a low desk, courtiers around him as he gazes toward the west with a firm, calculating expression.

dialogue.text: Mahmud Khalji, Sultan of Malwa, pushed east and west to hold his fragile sultanate together, his armies moving toward the lands of Mewar and its rising Rana.

i18n.hi: मालवा का सुल्तान महमूद ख़िलजी, अपनी नाज़ुक सल्तनत जोड़े रखने को पूरब‑पश्चिम धक्का दे रहा था, उसकी सेनाएँ उभरते राणा की भूमि मेवाड़ की ओर बढ़ रहीं थीं।

panels.shot: interior court shot at Chittor, three-quarter view, focused on Rana Kumbha
panels.action: In a pillared hall of Chittor, Rana Kumbha sits on a plain throne, scholars and warriors at his feet, one hand on a sheaf of palm-leaf manuscripts, the other on the hilt of his sword, his face calm yet alert.

dialogue.text: Rana Kumbhakarna Singh of Mewar, remembered as Kumbha, ruled a house that had survived centuries of wars; now he tightened its hold over Chittor, Kumbhalgarh and the passes between.

i18n.hi: मेवाड़ के राणा कुम्भकर्ण सिंह, यानी कुम्भा, उस वंश को चलाते थे जो सदियों की लड़ाइयाँ झेल चुका था; अब वह चित्तौड़, कुम्भलगढ़ और बीच की घाटियों पर पकड़ कसी जा रहे थे।

panels.shot: map-table close-up shot, hands from both sides pointing, symbolic rather than literal meeting
panels.action: Against a close-up of a map showing the Malwa plateau and Mewar’s hills, two different hands—one in Rajput bangles, one in a Sultan’s signet ring—point toward the same spot marked Sarangpur.

dialogue.text: Some campaigns began with raids and counter-raids along the frontier, but in 1437 the two rulers chose the open plain near Sarangpur in Malwa to test each other’s strength.

i18n.hi: कुछ मुहिमें सीमा पर छापों और जवाबी छापों से शुरू हुईं, पर १४३७ में दोनों शासकों ने मालवा के सारंगपुर के खुले मैदान में आमने‑सामने ताकत आज़माने का फैसला किया।

panels.shot: dawn battlefield wide shot, low horizon, silhouettes of armies assembling
panels.action: Under a pale dawn sky at Sarangpur, long lines of armoured horsemen, elephants and foot-soldiers gather on a broad plain, dust rising as both sides form up facing each other in tense silence.

dialogue.text: The inscriptions of Mewar and the later Persian histories agree on this much: the armies of Mewar and Malwa met near Sarangpur, and the day would belong to Rana Kumbha.

i18n.hi: मेवाड़ के अभिलेख और बाद की फ़ारसी तवारीख़ इस बात पर सहमत हैं: मेवाड़ और मालवा की सेनाएँ सारंगपुर के पास टकराईं, और वह दिन राणा कुम्भा के नाम रहा।

panels.shot: tight medium on Rana Kumbha on horseback, slight low angle
panels.action: Rana Kumbha, clad in mail with a simple turban-helmet, sits steady on his warhorse at the Mewar front, his eyes narrowed, right arm raised in a restrained signal to advance.

dialogue.speaker: rana_kumbha_and_mahmud_khalji_of_malwa
dialogue.text: Hold the line. Let the plain itself slow them.

i18n.hi: पंक्ति थामो। मैदान खुद उन्हें रेंगने दो।

panels.shot: dynamic tracking shot across the Malwa line, focused on Mahmud Khalji
panels.action: Mahmud Khalji rides along the Malwa front in rich, inlaid armour, his horse mid-stride, raising his sword in a rallying gesture as his troops lean forward, eager and tense.

dialogue.speaker: rana_kumbha_and_mahmud_khalji_of_malwa
dialogue.text: Press hard. Break them before the sun climbs high.

i18n.hi: ज़ोर लगाओ। धूप चढ़ने से पहले उनकी कमर तोड़ दो।

panels.shot: chaotic mid-wide battle shot, but composed, focusing on momentum rather than violence
panels.action: The two lines crash; horses rear, spears tilt, dust swirls thick, with Rana Kumbha’s banner just visible pushing forward as Malwa’s front ranks bend under the pressure.

dialogue.text: Chroniclers do not give numbers, but all agree that at Sarangpur the Malwa line broke; under the weight of Mewar’s charge and discipline, Mahmud Khalji’s army recoiled.

i18n.hi: इतिहासकारों ने आँकड़े नहीं छोड़े, पर सब मानते हैं कि सारंगपुर पर मालवा की पंक्ति टूटी; मेवाड़ के धावे और अनुशासन के भार से महमूद ख़िलजी की फ़ौज पीछे हट गई।

panels.shot: medium shot of Mahmud Khalji amidst retreating troops, three-quarter rear view
panels.action: Mahmud Khalji turns in his saddle, his horse half-pivoted, as men stream past him in disorder; his jaw is set, torn between rallying them and following the retreat.

dialogue.text: Persian histories written a century later, like Firishta’s, speak of Mahmud’s defeat and flight; Rajput tradition goes further, saying he could not escape the field at all.

i18n.hi: एक सदी बाद लिखी फ़ारसी किताबें, जैसे फ़िरिश्ता की, महमूद की हार और भागने को सँभालती हैं; राजपूत परंपरा इससे आगे बढ़कर कहती है कि वह मैदान से निकल ही नहीं पाया।

panels.shot: tight, tense shot in the melee, focused on Mahmud being surrounded, weapons lowered, no gore
panels.action: In the thinning dust, a ring of Mewar horsemen closes around Mahmud Khalji, their lances held level but not striking, as he pulls his horse to a halt, shoulders squared.

dialogue.text: According to the Kumbhalgarh inscription and later Rajput accounts, the Sultan was taken alive at Sarangpur—prized not as a trophy of blood, but as a living proof of victory.

i18n.hi: कुम्भलगढ़ के लेख और बाद की राजपूत कथाओं के मुताबिक सुल्तान सारंगपुर पर ज़िंदा पकड़ा गया – खून की निशानी नहीं, बल्कि जीत का साँस लेता हुआ सबूत।

panels.shot: medium shot of Rana Kumbha and a dismounted Mahmud facing each other, eye-level
panels.action: In a quiet patch of the battlefield after the fighting, Mahmud Khalji stands unarmed but upright, flanked by Mewar guards, as Rana Kumbha approaches on foot and studies him with a steady gaze.

dialogue.speaker: rana_kumbha_and_mahmud_khalji_of_malwa
dialogue.text: Today, the field is mine. Tomorrow, we both answer to time.

i18n.hi: आज मैदान मेरा है। कल, हम दोनों हिसाब वक्त से देंगे।

panels.shot: interior camp shot, lamplit, with Mahmud seated in guarded dignity
panels.action: Inside a large war tent lit by oil lamps, Mahmud Khalji sits on a carpet with his hands free, guarded but treated with formality, as a Mewar officer bows and departs with a message.

dialogue.text: Later Indo-Persian writers remember Mahmud’s setback but do not dwell on captivity; Rajput sources stress that he was held with honour, then allowed to return to Mandu.

i18n.hi: बाद के हिंद‑फ़ारसी लेखक महमूद की इस नाकामी को याद करते हैं पर क़ैद पर नहीं टिकते; राजपूत स्रोत बताते हैं कि उसे सम्मान के साथ रखा गया, फिर मण्डू लौटने दिया गया।

panels.shot: sunset long shot of a small escorted group riding away from the Mewar camp
panels.action: At sunset, a small escort of Mewar horsemen rides alongside Mahmud Khalji as he heads back across the plain, the distant outline of Mandu’s plateau barely visible on the horizon.

dialogue.text: Modern historians, reading both traditions, see the core event clearly—defeat at Sarangpur—but cannot fully measure how long or how tightly the Sultan was held.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक इतिहासकार दोनों परंपराएँ पढ़कर मूल घटना साफ़ देखते हैं – सारंगपुर की हार – पर यह नहीं नाप पाते कि सुल्तान कितने समय, कितनी सख़्ती से रोका गया।

panels.shot: grand wide shot of Chittor’s skyline with scaffolding around an emerging tall tower
panels.action: Back in Chittor, towering stone walls rise over the hills as masons work high on a new, many-storeyed victory tower, its unfinished face catching the harsh midday sun.

dialogue.text: In the years after Sarangpur, Kumbha’s realm grew surer; his inscriptions boast of victories, and Chittor’s famous Vijay Stambha rises from this wider culture of triumph and memory.

i18n.hi: सारंगपुर के बाद के वर्षों में कुम्भा का राज्य और दिलेर हुआ; उसके अभिलेख जीतों का बखान करते हैं, और चित्तौड़ का विख्यात विजय स्तम्भ इसी विजयोत्सव और स्मृति की संस्कृति से उगता है।

panels.shot: closer shot of the Vijay Stambha’s carved panels, angled upward
panels.action: The camera looks up the richly carved face of the Vijay Stambha, its niches filled with deities, warriors and inscriptions, the stone surface weathered but still sharp under a clear sky.

dialogue.text: Yet the tower is not a single news-sheet for Sarangpur alone; it gathers many claims, victories, gods and kings into one stone argument about who held this land.

i18n.hi: पर यह मीनार सिर्फ़ सारंगपुर की एक खबर नहीं; यह बहुत‑सी दावों, विजयाओं, देवताओं और राजाओं को एक पत्थर की दलील में जोड़ती है कि यह धरती किसकी थी।

panels.shot: study interior shot with a modern historian’s silhouette before photographs of inscriptions and Persian manuscripts, symbolic
panels.action: In a dim room, a lone figure sits at a desk strewn with photographs of Sanskrit inscriptions and Persian manuscripts, the light from a small lamp catching the Sanskrit and Arabic scripts side by side.

dialogue.text: Court poets praised their own patrons; later chroniclers wrote for different thrones. Today’s historians sift Kumbhalgarh’s inscription, Nizamuddin’s Tabaqat and Firishta’s tales, testing each against the other.

i18n.hi: दरबारी कवि अपने‑अपने सरदारों के गुण गाते रहे; बाद के इतिहासकार अलग दरबारों के लिए लिखते रहे। आज के शोधकर्ता कुम्भलगढ़ का शिलालेख, निज़ामुद्दीन की तबक़ात और फ़िरिश्ता की दास्तानें टटोलते हैं, एक को दूसरे पर परखते हुए।

panels.shot: dual close-up: Rana Kumbha’s sculpted face on a temple wall and a painted miniature of Mahmud Khalji, side by side
panels.action: A carved relief of Rana Kumbha’s profile on a temple wall faces a delicate miniature painting of Mahmud Khalji in a manuscript, the two images held side by side by unseen hands.

dialogue.text: Sarangpur did not make either man flawless; it made their choices visible—Kumbha’s new confidence in the hill-kingdom of Mewar, Mahmud’s need to rebuild Malwa after a public defeat.

i18n.hi: सारंगपुर ने न तो किसी को बेअिब बना दिया; इसने उनके फ़ैसले खुलकर दिखा दिए – मेवाड़ के पहाड़ी राज्य में कुम्भा का नया भरोसा, और खुली हार के बाद मालवा को फिर से जोड़ने की महमूद की मजबूरी।

panels.shot: final wide shot from high above Sarangpur’s plain, blending into the outline of the Vijay Stambha
panels.action: From high above, the quiet fields around Sarangpur stretch into the distance, and as the view slowly darkens, the silhouette of the Vijay Stambha rises ghostlike over the landscape.

dialogue.text: On that plain, a Sultan fell back and a Rana rose higher; their battle lives on only because stones, songs and chronicles still argue over what it meant, asking us to read them together.

i18n.hi: उस मैदान पर, एक सुल्तान पीछे हटा और एक राणा ऊँचा उठा; उनकी लड़ाई आज इसलिए ज़िंदा है कि पत्थर, गीत और इतिहास अभी भी उसके मायने पर झगड़ते हैं, और हमें उन्हें साथ‑साथ पढ़ने को बुलाते हैं।

title_i18n.en: Sarangpur and the Sultan Taken Alive
title_i18n.hi: सारंगपुर और ज़िंदा पकड़ा गया सुल्तान

subtitle_i18n.hi: मेवाड़ बनाम मालवा – जब सुल्तान हारकर लौटा
